title: Six-Point Programme publicly presented
detail: At an opposition convention in Lahore, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman outlined the Six Points as a constitutional programme for meaningful autonomy of East Pakistan.

title: Programme circulated across East Pakistan
detail: Party activists, students, and civic networks spread the Six-Point demands through meetings, leaflets, and public campaigns.

title: State response intensifies
detail: Authorities moved to suppress Six-Point mobilization through surveillance, arrests, and legal pressure on opposition leaders.

title: Six Points become central to autonomy politics
detail: The programme reshaped opposition discourse and linked constitutional debate with mass demands for regional rights and democratic accountability.

title: Legacy carried into mass uprising and liberation politics
detail: The Six-Point framework continued to influence mobilization strategies and political narratives leading up to 1971.
